title: Spotify Music Streaming: Complete Architecture
description: Design spotify music streaming with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a music streaming platform similar to Spotify that serves millions of users with personalized recommendations, playlist management, artist pages, and real-time playback statistics. The system must stream high-quality audio with gapless playback, generate daily personalized playlists like Discover Weekly, and track listening history to power collaborative and algorithmic recommendations.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Stream full songs and podcasts with adaptive bitrate based on network conditions
Generate personalized playlists (Discover Weekly, Release Radar, Daily Mix) based on listening history
Allow users to create, edit, and share public or private playlists with follow/like support
Search for artists, albums, tracks, podcasts, and lyrics with typo-tolerant matching
Display real-time listening statistics: top artists, recently played, and genre breakdowns
Support collaborative playlists where multiple users can add and reorder tracks
Download tracks and podcasts for offline listening with DRM protection and expiry
Queue management: play next, add to queue, and crossfade between tracks
Artist pages with discography, monthly listeners, related artists, and concert listings
Podcast management with episode progress tracking, subscription, and episode downloads

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Audio playback starts within 300ms of user action with no buffering stalls on 4G
99.99% availability for streaming endpoints with graceful degradation to cached content
Support 100 million monthly active users with 10 million concurrent streams
Recommendation generation completes within 4 hours for 400 million users nightly
Playback metadata (scrobbles, skips, completions) delivers to analytics within 5 seconds
Regional compliance for content licensing and copyright royalty reporting

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application that validates the Spotify music domain: catalog browsing, audio streaming, playlist CRUD, user preferences, and listening history. This validates recommendation data flow and playback tracking before splitting into services.

terms.term: Frontend
- React 18 with TypeScript
- Vite for build tooling
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- React Query for server state
Backend (ASP.NET Core)
- Minimal API or MVC Controllers
- Entity Framework Core for data access
- Azure SQL Database or AWS RDS for relational data
- Built-in DI, logging, and health checks
Infrastructure
- Azure App Service or AWS EC2/ECS
- Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for file assets
- Azure Monitor or AWS CloudWatch for logging
- Single database with tables for all domains

data.text: As traffic grows, split the monolith into independently scalable microservices. Each service owns its data and communicates via async messaging or REST/gRPC.

items: Media Service: Handles adaptive bitrate streaming using HLS or DASH, serves cached audio segments from edge CDN, and reports playback telemetry (start, pause, skip, complete) to analytics. Uses range requests for seeking within tracks.

Recommendation Service: Generates personalized playlists using collaborative filtering (user-user and item-item similarity), content-based filtering (audio features, genre, mood), and deep learning models trained on listening history. Stores embeddings in vector databases for similarity search.

Catalog Service: Manages artist profiles, album and track metadata, lyrics with synchronized timestamps, podcast episodes, and content availability by region. Powers search with typo-tolerant matching and autocomplete.

Playlist Service: Handles playlist CRUD with ordered track lists, collaborative editing with operational transforms to resolve concurrent reorders, follow/like counts, and public sharing links with embed support.

User Profile Service: Stores listening preferences, explicit likes, device registrations, download states for offline mode, and queue state per device. Tracks last played position per track for resume functionality.

Key Patterns
- Feature-based folder structure
- API Gateway as single entry point
- React Query for metadata caching with background refetch on focus
- Web Audio API for gapless playback and crossfade effects
- Service Worker for offline playback of downloaded tracks
